correctness.rationale: The inverse-image argument applies to every finite reset word, with no length restriction. In the frame rotated by the number t of preceding inverse a steps, inverse b copies the membership of t mod n into t−1 mod n. From the terminal singleton {r}, the first additions must therefore be r−1, r−2, …, r−(n−1), even if later inverse b steps delete positions. The successive addition times have residues decreasing by one and thus are at least n−1 rotations apart. There must also be at least n−1 inverse b steps. Equality in both counts forces the initial addition at t=0, all gaps exactly n−1, and no redundant steps; conversely those steps reach Q. This includes n=2, where the equality word is b. Strict positivity makes equality in weighted cost equivalent to equality in both counts. The finite subset searches described in the frozen verification are corroborative, not the basis for the general conclusion.
